meta.titre: The Paris Peace Settlement at Advanced Level: aims, treaties and the debate on its success
meta.sous_theme: Aims of the Allied leaders, the Treaty of Versailles and its critics

sections.contenu_markdown: The decisions taken in Paris in 1919 changed the map of the world, including the map of Cameroon. Germany lost its colony of Kamerun, which Britain and France had occupied during the war, divided formally in 1919 and ruled as League of Nations mandates from 1922.At Advanced Level you are asked to go further than listing the terms: you must explain what each leader wanted, why Germany felt wronged, and whether the settlement succeeded. This course gives the facts and the way to argue them.

items: The First World War ended with the armistice of 11 November 1918.
Woodrow Wilson, the American president, announced his Fourteen Points in January 1918, including self-determination and a league of nations.
Reparations are payments made by a defeated state for the damage caused by a war.
Self-determination means that a people should be able to choose the government under which it lives.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### Aims of the leaders
| Leader | Country | Main aim |
|---|---|---|
| Woodrow Wilson | USA | A just peace based on self-determination and a League of Nations to keep the peace |
| Georges Clemenceau | France | Security against a new German attack; a weakened Germany |
| David Lloyd George | Britain | A peace that protected the empire and the navy, kept British public opinion satisfied and did not ruin German trade |
| Vittorio Orlando | Italy | Territory promised to Italy in a secret treaty of 1915 |

### The Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919)
- **War guilt**: Article 231 stated that Germany accepted responsibility for the loss and damage suffered by the Allies. It was the legal basis for reparations.
- **Reparations**: the amount was not fixed in the treaty. It was set in 1921 at 132 billion gold marks.
- **Territory**: Alsace-Lorraine returned to France; the Saar was placed under League administration for fifteen years; Poland received land giving it access to the sea; the German colonies became League mandates.
- **Military**: the army was limited to 100,000 men, with no air force, and the Rhineland was demilitarised and occupied by the Allies for up to fifteen years.
- **Union with Austria** was forbidden.

### The other treaties
Separate treaties were made with Austria (Saint-Germain, 1919), Bulgaria (Neuilly, 1919), Hungary (Trianon, 1920) and the Ottoman Empire (Sevres, 1920). Turkish nationalists under Mustafa Kemal rejected Sevres, and the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 replaced it.

### Achievements and weaknesses
| Achievements | Weaknesses |
|---|---|
| The League of Nations was created and its Covenant was part of the treaties | Germany was not allowed to negotiate and called the treaty a 'diktat' |
| New states such as Poland and Czechoslovakia appeared, partly on the principle of self-determination | Self-determination was applied unevenly: German speakers were included in other states and union with Austria was banned |
| France recovered Alsace-Lorraine and Germany was disarmed | The American Senate refused to ratify the treaty, so the USA did not join the League |
| The peace ended the war and was less severe than the treaty Germany had imposed on Russia in 1918 | Italy felt cheated of promised gains, and reparations caused lasting bitterness |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks why Germany resented the settlement.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Select the terms that touched German pride and economy: war guilt, reparations, loss of land and colonies, disarmament and exclusion from the talks. Explain why each hurt and say which hurt most.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks for the greatest achievement, or whether the settlement succeeded.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Choose criteria (peace-keeping, fairness, stability, new institutions), judge the settlement against each, and finish with a verdict. Do not just list terms.

sections.enonce_markdown: Assess the view that the Treaty of Versailles was too harsh on Germany.

etapes.justification: 'Too harsh' needs a standard before it can be judged.
etapes.resultat_markdown: I will judge harshness by the loss of land, money and power, and compare with other treaties of the time.

etapes.justification: Facts from the treaty support the claim.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Germany lost land in Europe and all its colonies, had its army limited to 100,000 men, had to accept Article 231 and pay reparations, and was not allowed to negotiate.

etapes.justification: A balanced answer must test the claim.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Germany stayed united and kept most of its territory and industry; the Allies did not occupy the whole of Germany or divide it; the treaty imposed on Russia by Germany in 1918 had been harsher in the land it took.

etapes.action: Explain the effect on German opinion.
etapes.justification: The question concerns perception as well as terms.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Most Germans saw the treaty as a 'diktat' and Article 231 as an insult, so the settlement left a feeling of injustice even if some terms were moderate.

etapes.justification: The conclusion must answer the question.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The treaty was harsh in the way it was imposed and in the burden of reparations and guilt, but it was not so severe that it destroyed Germany.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer (key points)**: The Treaty of Versailles was harsh in some respects: Germany lost land and colonies, was disarmed, was made to accept responsibility for the war and was excluded from the talks. However, Germany remained a united and powerful country, and the treaty was no harsher than the one Germany itself imposed on Russia in 1918. The greatest weakness was that it was harsh enough to cause lasting resentment but not strong enough to keep Germany weak, and this reduced its chance of lasting.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1918."
items.pourquoi_faux: The armistice was in November 1918. The treaty was signed on 28 June 1919.
items.correction_markdown: Write November 1918 for the armistice and June 1919 for the treaty.

items.pourquoi_faux: Article 231 stated responsibility. The sum was decided later, in 1921.
items.correction_markdown: Write that Article 231 was the basis for reparations and that the amount was set in 1921.

items.erreur_markdown: "The Treaty of Versailles dealt with all the defeated powers."
items.pourquoi_faux: Versailles dealt with Germany only. Austria, Hungary, Bulgaria and the Ottoman Empire had separate treaties.
items.correction_markdown: Name the right treaty for each defeated state.

items.erreur_markdown: "Wilson achieved all his aims and the USA joined the League."
items.pourquoi_faux: Wilson had to compromise with Clemenceau and Lloyd George, and the American Senate refused to ratify the treaty.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the USA did not join the League of Nations and that Wilson's aims were only partly achieved.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the three leaders usually called the 'Big Three' at the Paris Peace Conference and the country of each.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each correct pair: **Woodrow Wilson (USA), Georges Clemenceau (France), David Lloyd George (Britain)**.

items.enonce_markdown: Explain why Italy was dissatisfied with the peace settlement.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for developed points: (1) Italy had joined the Allies in 1915 after a secret treaty promising territory; (2) at Paris Wilson's principle of self-determination and the claims of other states prevented Italy from obtaining all it expected; (3) Italians spoke of a 'mutilated victory'; (4) this resentment helped nationalists in Italy. **The answer must link the promise, the disappointment and the political result.**

items.enonce_markdown: Discuss the view that the League of Nations was the most important achievement of the Paris Peace Conference.
items.solution_markdown: Plan: For: the League was a new institution to settle disputes by discussion and to administer mandates, and its Covenant was included in the treaties. Against: it was weakened by the absence of the USA and the lack of an army; other achievements such as new states and the return of Alsace-Lorraine mattered at the time. Judgement: **the League was the most original achievement, but its importance depended on whether it worked, and its weaknesses limited its success.**

items_markdown: The Allied leaders had different aims: Wilson wanted a just peace and a League, Clemenceau wanted security, Lloyd George wanted a moderate settlement protecting British interests.
The Treaty of Versailles (28 June 1919) included war guilt (Article 231), reparations (fixed at 132 billion gold marks in 1921), territorial losses, disarmament and the Rhineland clauses.
Separate treaties were made with Austria, Bulgaria, Hungary and the Ottoman Empire; Sevres was replaced by Lausanne in 1923.
Germany resented the exclusion from the talks, war guilt, reparations and the unequal use of self-determination.
Achievements: the League and new states; weaknesses: resentment, American absence and uneven application of principles.
In 'greatest achievement' or 'assess' questions, use criteria and give a reasoned verdict.
